newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel confident banks will accept debt plan.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel confident banks will accept debt plan.

text.p: The managing director of Eurotunnel said he was confident creditor banks would accept a major debt restructuring plan for the channel tunnel operator which was overwhelmingly approved by shareholders late Thursday.
"We think they will accept it (the plan). In each city where we have been we have received a very positive reception," Georges-Christian Chazot told Reuters at a shareholders' meeting in Paris.
The steering group of Eurotunnel's 174 lenders approved the debt plan in principle. Now all individual lenders must also accept the deal.

Chazot said he was in Tokyo last week to present the restructuring plan to Japanese banks and executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle visited New York two weeks ago. Eurotunnel executives have also met bank officials in Paris, London, Milan and Frankfurt.
Chazot said some banks might wonder whether they had given up too much under the deal, but that was to be expected.

The agreement to restructure 70 billion francs of junior debt would cut Eurotunnel's interest charges to 3.2 billion francs this year from 5.7 billion paid in 1996, giving the tunnel operator breathing room. But it would cut shareholders' equity to 54.5 percent with the creditor banks taking 45.5 percent.
Ponsolle told shareholders at the meeting that the banks were giving up 22 billion francs of interest payments over seven years under the terms of the plan.
